missed.title: Concurrency hazards in token re-issuance
missed.reasoning: The RCA doesn't address concurrent request handling where multiple requests from the same session could trigger simultaneous token re-issuance, leading to token version conflicts or race conditions in cookie setting.
missed.suggested_action: Add mutex or atomic state management around token refresh per session to prevent concurrent re-issuance.

missed.title: Error handling in response-mutating layer
missed.reasoning: No coverage of failure scenarios in the response-mutating middleware (e.g., JWT generation failure during refresh). This could leave responses incomplete or cause panics.
missed.suggested_action: Define comprehensive error handling paths for middleware failures, including fallback to original response and structured logging.

missed.title: Cookie collision risk with PIN paths
missed.reasoning: RCA mentions cookie helpers but doesn't verify absence of naming conflicts between idle-timeout cookies and existing PIN cookies from admin.rs, risking overwrites or client-side conflicts.
missed.suggested_action: Audit all cookie namespaces in auth/admin.rs and ensure new cookie uses distinct name with conflict analysis.

missed.title: Deployment rollback hazards
missed.reasoning: Ignores backward compatibility during rollback: new sliding-window tokens issued during deployment would become invalid if rolling back to fixed-window version, causing immediate session expirations.
missed.suggested_action: Implement versioned JWT claims or deployment-stage aware token validation to support safe rollbacks.

missed.title: Clock skew amplification in distributed systems
missed.reasoning: While clock skew is mentioned, RCA doesn't address how skew greater than idle_timeout_secs could cause simultaneous valid/invalid token states across horizontally scaled instances.
missed.suggested_action: Add NTP enforcement checks in deployment pipeline and document skew tolerance limits in validation logic.

misclassified.reasoning: Classified as indirect but is critical path for sliding-window validity checks; skew tolerance must be explicitly designed into refresh logic.

misclassified.item: JWT secret rotation grace period interaction
misclassified.reasoning: Downplayed as design choice when mid-rotation refreshes could create tokens valid under both old/new secrets, weakening cryptographic hygiene.

missed.title: HashMap DoS vulnerabilities
missed.reasoning: In-memory HashMaps for attempt tracking are susceptible to memory exhaustion attacks via malicious staff_id proliferation. RCA mentions unbounded growth but not active exploitation risks.
missed.suggested_action: Implement staff_id validation or LRU eviction with alarms for abnormal growth patterns.

missed.title: Atomicity gaps in PIN rotation
missed.reasoning: No discussion of transactional integrity between PIN change, audit logging, and counter reset. Network partition during change_staff_pin_safe could leave system in inconsistent state.
missed.suggested_action: Add compensating transactions or idempotency tokens for rotation workflow.

missed.title: Email delivery observability gaps
missed.reasoning: While transport verification is noted, RCA omits real-time monitoring for email delivery failures and alerting when helpdesk@ messages aren't received.
missed.suggested_action: Integrate with email provider webhooks for delivery receipts and add Prometheus alerts for undelivered PIN rotations.

missed.title: Staff_id enumeration via timing attacks
missed.reasoning: Per-staff-id rate-limiting introduces side-channel where response times could reveal valid staff_ids. Not mitigated in proposal.
missed.suggested_action: Add constant-time hash comparison or request batching to obscure staff_id validity.

missed.title: Cold start state loss hazards
missed.reasoning: In-memory state for attempt counters is lost on restart, allowing lockout bypass if crashes occur after failed attempts but before rotation.
missed.suggested_action: Document behavior in runbooks and add startup reconciliation with audit_log.

misclassified.reasoning: Misclassified as V1-only issue; cooldown bypass creates new attack vector for email flooding if attacker triggers repeated lockouts.
Treated as implementation choice when absence fundamentally blocks feature delivery. Should be elevated to deployment prerequisite.

cross_rca_interactions.title: Cookie header collision in response chains
cross_rca_interactions.reasoning: W1-S5's response-mutating middleware sets auth cookies concurrently with W1-S6's potential cookie operations during PIN resets. Uncoordinated Set-Cookie headers could exceed browser limits or cause non-deterministic precedence.

cross_rca_interactions.title: Shared secret rotation hazards
cross_rca_interactions.reasoning: W1-S5's JWT secret rotation design (always use current secret) conflicts with W1-S6's PIN reset emails containing time-sensitive credentials. Coordinated rotation required to avoid PINs becoming invalid during rotation windows.

cross_rca_interactions.title: Audit log write amplification synergy
cross_rca_interactions.reasoning: Both features increase audit_log volume: W1-S5 through explicit expiry logging, W1-S6 through PIN rotations. Combined load could exceed current PostgreSQL instance capacity during peak events.

blocker_reasoning: Both RCAs miss critical P1 implementation hazards (concurrency, error handling, security) and misclassify security-sensitive items. Cross-RCA interactions introduce unaddressed systemic risks. Must address gaps before proceeding to implementation.
